reviews.quote: Aggregated scoring places it at around 76% overall, indicating a solid but not flawless package.
An ineffective cooling system, slow SSD hampered by bloatware, bulky design, and short battery life make the Neo 16 AI a hard sell.

professional.note: No dedicated pro review found for the Neo 18 non-AI PHN18-72; ratings inferred from the NBC-reviewed PHN16-73 Neo platform (same CPU/GPU stack, larger chassis). Honest null — no numeric score exists for this exact config.

praises: 18" 240Hz screen at ~$3,240 sale is one of the cheapest big-screen 5070 laptops in Canada
24-core Ultra 9 275HX is a workstation-class CPU at a gaming price
Roomy chassis runs the 5070 cool and quiet in Performance mode (Neo platform pattern)
Full numeric keypad + wide deck — comfortable for long sessions
USB4/TB4, SD reader and RJ-45; RAM/storage user-upgradeable
complaints: 3.5 kg + 400W-class brick: this is a desktop replacement, not a laptop you carry
RTX 5070's 8GB VRAM is the weak link vs 12GB 5070 Ti at similar street prices
Matte IPS panel is average — mediocre brightness and contrast next to OLED rivals
Acer bloatware and PredatorSense quirks on first boot (line-wide complaint)
Short battery life; 18" HX machines realistically live plugged in

design_philosophy: The Neo 18 stretches the Neo 16 formula to 18 inches: same flagship CPU and mid-tier GPUs in a desktop-replacement chassis where cooling headroom and screen real estate replace portability. This 5070/32GB tier is the value entry to big-screen Predator gaming — you buy it for the 18" 240Hz canvas and the 24-core CPU, accepting the 8GB-VRAM GPU.
